question: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q3 FY2027 earnings release? (Gross margin (GAAP))

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 26, 2026) management said gross margin would bottom in Q4 FY27 at 71-72% because of memory prices, then recover to 72-73% in FY28. That implies a 71.5% midpoint for the Q4 guide. GAAP and non-GAAP have been identical (75.0% in Q2; 74.0% guided for both in Q3). Memory costs still rising and commitments jumping to $279B point down (70.5-71.0); executed price increases and conservative guiding point up (72.0-72.5). Polymarket only prices Q3 actual non-GAAP margin (~87% on 73-75%), which is consistent with the 74% Q3 guide; I found no market on the Q4 guide itself.
calls.dossier:
- Q2 FY27 press release (Aug 26, 2026): Q2 GAAP GM 75.0%, non-GAAP GM 75.0%. Q3 outlook: GAAP and non-GAAP GM 74.0% +/-50bp; revenue $108.0B +/-2%; GAAP opex ~$9.2B.
- Q2 FY27 earnings call (reported by TIKR and Trefis Nov 6, 2026; a GamesReviews headline found in search but not opened): management said GM would 'bottom at 71% to 72% in the fourth quarter before recovering to 72-73% in fiscal 2028', with memory prices the main driver and executed price increases taking effect in Q1 FY28. Sources do not say whether this was GAAP or non-GAAP, but the two have been identical recently.
- Q2 CFO commentary (SEC 8-K): supply/purchase commitments rose from $119B to $279B, mainly memory; no explicit Q4 margin text in the written commentary.
- Trefis (Nov 6, 2026): memory prices rose more than expected and are still climbing.
- Kress quoted: 'We want to be direct about this, rather than let it linger as an open question.'
- Earlier target was 'mid-70s' for FY27; that target was abandoned due to memory costs.
- Vera Rubin expected to be about 20% of data center revenue in Q3 FY27 (first shipment quarter); a new-product ramp can weigh on margins.
- NVIDIA guides GM as a point +/-50bp, usually in round 0.5 increments; same figure for GAAP and non-GAAP in recent quarters.
- Status quo: the Q4 guide matches the stated 71-72% trough (midpoint 71.5).
- Resolves off the midpoint of the GAAP GM range in the Outlook section of the Q3 FY27 press release (expected Nov 17, 2026), rounded to 0.1%; not off the call commentary.
- Event window: single release on Nov 17, 2026; as of Nov 8 the release has not happened.
- Searched but not found: any mid-quarter management update on margins, sell-side consensus for the Q4 GM guide, a betting market on the Q4 guide (Polymarket only prices Q3 actual non-GAAP GM).

calls.reasoning: On the Q2 FY27 call (Aug 2026), management explicitly said Q4 FY27 gross margin is expected to bottom in the 71-72% range due to extreme memory pricing, with FY28 recovering to 72-73%. NVIDIA's formal guides have historically landed on previously signalled verbal targets, and GAAP and non-GAAP have recently been guided identically, so a '71.5% ± 50bp' guide is the modal outcome. Downside: memory costs rising beyond expectations (Kress said 'headed even higher') could push the guide to 71.0% or lower; upside: price increases or mix could lift it toward 72%. Market check: no human market prices Q4 guidance; the Polymarket contracts are on Q3 actual non-GAAP GM (73-75% at 0.87, ~$4.9k volume), consistent with the 74% Q3 guide, so they are not an anchor.

- Q2 FY27 call highlights (Yahoo Finance, Aug 2026): Q4 FY27 gross margin 'expected to bottom in the 71% to 72% range'; FY2028 GM 'expected to settle at 72% to 73%'; decline attributed to 'extreme memory pricing conditions'.

calls.reconciliation: All three runs share the same facts: Q2 call guidance of a 71-72% bottom in Q4, GAAP equal to non-GAAP in the latest guide, and no update after August. There was no factual dispute. The only judgment difference was tail width (1.2 vs 1.5). I kept the 71.5 mode and the runs' reference class, and set a slightly down-skewed width of 1.4 to reflect the continued rise in memory costs and the historical GAAP gap below non-GAAP. I retrieved nothing myself on this run.
